P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: No. Israel abolished most of its foreign-exchange controls in the 1990s, and there is no surrender or conversion requirement for foreign receipts.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Freelancers open a file with the Israel Tax Authority, covering VAT, income tax and National Insurance, as either an osek patur (exempt dealer) below the turnover ceiling or an osek murshe (licensed dealer) above it. The 2026 ceiling is reported as ₪120,000 or about ₪122,833; sources conflict. Certain professions (e.g. lawyers, doctors, architects) cannot use osek patur. Above the ceiling you must re-register as osek murshe and charge 18% VAT.

sources.title: Osek Patur vs Osek Murshe: Israel's ₪120,000 Freelancer VAT Threshold Explained
sources.quote: The 2026 Threshold: ₪120,000 ​ The osek patur revenue ceiling has been held at ₪120,000 in annual turnover for several consecutive years running through 2026.

sources.title: Freelancer Invoicing & Tax Deductions Israel 2026 (CWS Israel)
sources.quote: An Osek Patur stays below the 2026 revenue ceiling of approximately ₪122,833 and is exempt from charging or reclaiming VAT on Israeli transactions.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Israeli tax residents are taxed on worldwide income. Individual rates are graduated up to 47%, plus a 3% surtax above ILS 721,560, for a maximum of 50%; an extra 2% applies to certain capital income above that threshold. Self-employed people also pay National Insurance (not captured).

sources.quote: Israeli tax residents are taxable on their worldwide income.

sources.title: Israel - Individual - Taxes on personal income
sources.quote: Additionally, a 3% surtax applies on annual taxable income exceeding ILS 721,560, resulting in a 50% maximum income tax rate.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is 18% (from 1 January 2025, up from 17%). Exports of goods and certain services are zero-rated. Osek patur freelancers below the turnover ceiling (see L1) do not charge VAT. Invoices above ₪5,000 before VAT need a Tax Authority allocation number in 2026.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: The Protection of Privacy Law 5741-1981 and its regulations apply, under the Israel Privacy Authority. Amendment 13, effective 14 August 2025, narrowed database registration to data brokers and large public bodies and added DPO requirements in some cases. It also broadened 'especially sensitive data'.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Physical or digital goods on Etsy (Etsy seller payments are available here). (6) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Fully localized'). (7) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
